title: Written Calculations
description: Using column methods for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, and understanding the order of operations (BIDMAS).

notes.heading: Place Value and Column Addition
notes.body:
Every digit in a number has a value that depends on its position. Understanding place value is the foundation for every written calculation.

📌 Definition
Place value is the value of a digit based on where it sits in a number. In the number $3\,462$:
$$3\,462 = 3\,000 + 400 + 60 + 2$$
The $3$ is in the thousands column, the $4$ is in the hundreds column, the $6$ is in the tens column, and the $2$ is in the ones column.

🔑 How Column Addition Works
1. Write the numbers one above the other with digits lined up by place value.
2. Start adding from the right-hand (ones) column.
3. If a column totals $10$ or more, write down the ones digit and carry the tens digit to the next column on the left.
4. Repeat for each column, remembering to include any carried digits.

💡 Worked Example
Find $478 + 296$.

Step 1: Ones column
$$8 + 6 = 14$$
Write $4$, carry $1$.

Step 2: Tens column
$$7 + 9 + 1 = 17$$
Write $7$, carry $1$.

Step 3: Hundreds column
$$4 + 2 + 1 = 7$$

So $478 + 296 = 774$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always line up digits by place value, not by the left-hand edge.
• A carry happens whenever a column sum is $10$ or more.
• Addition is commutative: $a + b = b + a$.

✅ Check
Estimate first: $478 + 296 \approx 500 + 300 = 800$. The exact answer $774$ is close to $800$, so it is sensible.

notes.heading: Column Subtraction and Borrowing
notes.body:
Subtraction finds the difference between two numbers. When the top digit in a column is smaller than the bottom digit, we borrow from the next column to the left.

📌 Definition
The difference between two numbers is what you get when you subtract the smaller from the larger:
$$\text{difference} = \text{larger number} - \text{smaller number}$$

🔑 How Borrowing Works
1. Start from the right-hand (ones) column.
2. If the top digit is too small, borrow $1$ from the next column on the left. That left digit decreases by $1$, and the current top digit increases by $10$.
3. Subtract in each column.
4. Sometimes you need to borrow across a zero — this is called exchanging through zero.

💡 Worked Example
Find $6\,205 - 2\,478$.

Step 1: Ones column
$5 - 8$ is not possible, so borrow from the tens column. The $0$ tens cannot lend, so we must exchange through zero from the hundreds column.

$6\,205$ becomes:
• Hundreds: $2 \to 1$
• Tens: $0 \to 10$, then lend $1$ to the ones column, so tens become $9$ and ones become $15$.

Now subtract:
• Ones: $15 - 8 = 7$
• Tens: $9 - 7 = 2$
• Hundreds: $1 - 4$ is not possible, so borrow from thousands:
  - Thousands: $6 \to 5$
  - Hundreds: $1 \to 11$
• Hundreds: $11 - 4 = 7$
• Thousands: $5 - 2 = 3$

So $6\,205 - 2\,478 = 3\,727$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to reduce the digit you borrowed from. If you borrow $1$ from the tens column, you must reduce that tens digit by $1$ before subtracting.

✅ Tip
You can check a subtraction by adding the answer back to the number you subtracted:
$$3\,727 + 2\,478 = 6\,205 \quad \checkmark$$

notes.heading: Short and Long Multiplication
notes.body:
Multiplication is repeated addition. Written methods let us multiply large numbers quickly and accurately.

📌 Definition
The product of two numbers is the result of multiplying them:
$$\text{product} = a \times b$$

🔑 Short Multiplication
Use short multiplication when multiplying by a single digit.
1. Multiply each digit of the top number by the single digit.
2. Work from right to left.
3. Carry any tens to the next column.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Short multiplication
Find $347 \times 6$.

• $6 \times 7 = 42$: write $2$, carry $4$
• $6 \times 4 = 24$, plus $4$ carried $= 28$: write $8$, carry $2$
• $6 \times 3 = 18$, plus $2$ carried $= 20$

So $347 \times 6 = 2\,082$.

🔑 Long Multiplication
Use long multiplication when multiplying by a number with two or more digits.
1. Multiply by the ones digit of the bottom number to get the first partial product.
2. Multiply by the tens digit and write this second partial product one place to the left (or add a zero in the units column as a placeholder).
3. Continue for each digit.
4. Add the partial products together.

💡 Worked Example 2 — Long multiplication
Find $34 \times 27$.

First multiply by $7$:
$$34 \times 7 = 238$$

Then multiply by $20$:
$$34 \times 20 = 680$$

Add the partial products:
$$238 + 680 = 918$$

So $34 \times 27 = 918$.

⚠️ Common Misconception
When multiplying by the tens digit, remember you are really multiplying by $20$, not by $2$. The second partial product must be shifted one place to the left.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiplication is commutative: $a \times b = b \times a$.
• Multiplication is associative: $(a \times b) \times c = a \times (b \times c)$.
• Always estimate to check: $34 \times 27 \approx 30 \times 30 = 900$, and $918$ is close.

notes.heading: Short and Long Division
notes.body:
Division splits a number into equal parts. The two main written methods are short division (the bus-stop method) and long division.

📌 Definition
$$\text{quotient} = \text{dividend} \div \text{divisor}$$
When numbers do not divide exactly, the amount left over is called the remainder:
$$\text{dividend} = (\text{divisor} \times \text{quotient}) + \text{remainder}$$

🔑 Short Division (Bus-Stop Method)
Use short division when dividing by a single digit.
1. Work from left to right.
2. Divide each digit (including any carried remainder).
3. Write the quotient digit above and carry any remainder to the next column.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Short division
Find $875 \div 5$.

• $8 \div 5 = 1$ remainder $3$: write $1$, carry $3$
• $37 \div 5 = 7$ remainder $2$: write $7$, carry $2$
• $25 \div 5 = 5$: write $5$

So $875 \div 5 = 175$.

🔑 Long Division
Use long division when dividing by a number with two or more digits. Follow the sequence: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.

💡 Worked Example 2 — Long division
Find $672 \div 16$.

Step 1: $67 \div 16 = 4$ (since $16 \times 4 = 64$). Write $4$ above.
Step 2: Subtract $64$ from $67$: $67 - 64 = 3$.
Step 3: Bring down the $2$ to make $32$.
Step 4: $32 \div 16 = 2$. Write $2$ above.

So $672 \div 16 = 42$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A remainder can be written as:
  - "r" followed by the number, e.g. $17 \div 5 = 3$ r $2$
  - a fraction, e.g. $17 \div 5 = 3\frac{2}{5}$
  - a decimal, e.g. $17 \div 5 = 3.4$
• Check division by multiplying back: $175 \times 5 = 875$.

✅ Tip
If a division does not look right, estimate first. $672 \div 16 \approx 700 \div 20 = 35$, so $42$ is reasonable.

notes.heading: Order of Operations — BIDMAS
notes.body:
When a calculation contains more than one operation, the order in which you work matters. BIDMAS tells you the correct order.

📌 Definition
BIDMAS is an acronym for the order of operations:
\begin{aligned}
&\text{B} && \text{Brackets} \\
&\text{I} && \text{Indices (powers and roots)} \\
&\text{D} && \text{Division} \\
&\text{M} && \text{Multiplication} \\
&\text{A} && \text{Addition} \\
&\text{S} && \text{Subtraction}
\end{aligned}
Division and multiplication have equal priority and are done left to right. Addition and subtraction also have equal priority and are done left to right.

💡 Worked Example 1
Calculate $3 + 4 \times 5$.

Multiplication comes before addition:
$$4 \times 5 = 20$$
$$3 + 20 = 23$$

So $3 + 4 \times 5 = 23$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Working from left to right regardless of operation:
$$3 + 4 = 7 \text{, then } 7 \times 5 = 35 \quad \text{(WRONG)}$$
The correct answer is $23$.

💡 Worked Example 2
Calculate $(3 + 4) \times 5$.

Brackets come first:
$$3 + 4 = 7$$
$$7 \times 5 = 35$$

So $(3 + 4) \times 5 = 35$. The brackets change the answer completely.

💡 Worked Example 3
Calculate $24 \div 6 + 3 \times 2$.

Division and multiplication before addition, working left to right:
$$24 \div 6 = 4$$
$$3 \times 2 = 6$$
$$4 + 6 = 10$$

So $24 \div 6 + 3 \times 2 = 10$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always do brackets first.
• Indices (powers) are next.
• Then division and multiplication, left to right.
• Finally addition and subtraction, left to right.
• Brackets can be nested; do the innermost brackets first.

notes.heading: Working with Powers and Roots
notes.body:
Powers, also called indices, are a quick way to write repeated multiplication. They appear in the "I" of BIDMAS, so they must be calculated before multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction.

📌 Definition
A power tells you how many times a number is multiplied by itself:
$$a^n = a \times a \times a \times \cdots \times a \quad \text{($n$ times)}$$
Here $a$ is called the base and $n$ is called the index or exponent.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Evaluating powers
Calculate $2^5$.

$$2^5 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 32$$

Calculate $5^3$.

$$5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$$

🔑 Squares and Cubes
Squaring a number means multiplying it by itself:
$$4^2 = 4 \times 4 = 16$$

Cubing a number means multiplying it by itself three times:
$$4^3 = 4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$$

🔑 Square Roots
The square root of a number is the value that, when multiplied by itself, gives the original number:
$$\sqrt{36} = 6 \text{ because } 6 \times 6 = 36$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — BIDMAS with powers
Calculate $3 + 2^3 \times 4$.

Step 1: Indices
$$2^3 = 8$$

Step 2: Multiplication
$$8 \times 4 = 32$$

Step 3: Addition
$$3 + 32 = 35$$

So $3 + 2^3 \times 4 = 35$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Multiplying the base by the exponent. For example:
$$2^5 \neq 2 \times 5 = 10 \quad \text{(WRONG)}$$
The correct value is $2^5 = 32$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $a^2$ is read as "$a$ squared".
• $a^3$ is read as "$a$ cubed".
• $\sqrt{a}$ is the positive square root of $a$.
• Any non-zero number to the power of $0$ equals $1$, e.g. $7^0 = 1$.

notes.heading: Estimation, Word Problems and Checking
notes.body:
Estimation means finding an approximate answer quickly. It is one of the best ways to check whether a calculated answer is sensible.

📌 Definition
An estimate is a rough calculation, usually found by rounding numbers to one significant figure or to a convenient value.

🔑 How to Estimate
1. Round each number to one significant figure (or a nearby easy number).
2. Do the simplified calculation.
3. Compare the estimate with your exact answer.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Estimating a product
Estimate $497 \times 6$.

Round $497$ to $500$:
$$497 \times 6 \approx 500 \times 6 = 3\,000$$

The exact answer is $497 \times 6 = 2\,982$, which is very close to the estimate.

🔑 Choosing the Correct Operation
In word problems, look for keywords:
• Addition: total, altogether, combined, sum, increase
• Subtraction: difference, remaining, decrease, how many more, how much less
• Multiplication: product, each, groups of, total when there are equal groups
• Division: shared equally, per, how many in each group, quotient

💡 Worked Example 2 — Word problem
A school orders $15$ boxes of pencils. Each box contains $24$ pencils. How many pencils are there in total?

There are $15$ equal groups of $24$, so multiply:
$$15 \times 24 = 360$$

The school receives $360$ pencils.

✅ Check
Estimate: $15 \times 24 \approx 20 \times 20 = 400$. The exact answer $360$ is close to $400$, so it is reasonable.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always read word problems twice: once for the story, once for the numbers.
• Estimate before you calculate to predict the answer.
• Check afterwards by reversing the operation or rounding.
• If your exact answer is very different from your estimate, check your working for a place-value or arithmetic error.

flashcards.example: $58 + 27$: $8 + 7 = 15$, write $5$ and carry $1$ to the tens column.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit $7$ in the number $5\,748$?
questions.explanation: The digit $7$ is in the hundreds column, so its value is $700$.
Subtract with borrowing, including exchanging through zero: ones become $15$, tens become $9$, hundreds become $11$ after borrowing. Answer: $3\,727$.
Long division: $67 \div 16 = 4$ remainder $3$, bring down $2$ to make $32$, then $32 \div 16 = 2$. Answer: $42$.
Multiplication has higher priority than addition: $3 \times 6 = 18$, then $5 + 18 = 23$.
Brackets first: $8 + 4 = 12$. Then multiply: $12 \times 3 = 36$. Finally subtract: $36 - 5 = 31$.
Division and multiplication before addition, working left to right: $24 \div 6 = 4$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$. Then $4 + 6 = 10$.
Indices first: $2^3 = 8$. Then multiply: $8 \times 4 = 32$. Finally add: $3 + 32 = 35$.
$20 + 10 \div 2 = 20 + 5 = 25$. The other options give $23$, $35$, and $30$ respectively.

questions.stem: A school orders $15$ boxes of pencils. Each box has $24$ pencils. How many pencils are there in total?
questions.explanation: There are $15$ equal groups of $24$, so multiply: $15 \times 24 = (15 \times 20) + (15 \times 4) = 300 + 60 = 360$.

questions.stem: A shop sells notebooks in packs of $6$ for £$8$ and single notebooks for £$1.50$ each. A class needs $50$ notebooks. What is the cheapest way to buy them?
questions.explanation: $8$ packs give $48$ notebooks for £$8 \times 8 = 64$. Two more singles cost £$2 \times 1.50 = 3$, giving a total of £$67$, which is cheaper than the other options.

questions.stem: A rectangular hall is $18$ m long and $12$ m wide. It is divided into $8$ equal sections. What is the area of each section?
questions.explanation: First find the total area: $18 \times 12 = 216$ m$^2$. Then divide by $8$ equal sections: $216 \div 8 = 27$ m$^2$ per section. The distractor $216$ m$^2$ is the total area, not the area of one section.
